status: optional Rust planner patch; default vendor unchanged

protocol.scope: Expose semantic GROUPING_ID bits while preserving duplicate grouping-set rows; test unsigned storage widths, signed BIGINT output, NULL, empty input and HAVING.
protocol.boundary: 64 columns plus duplicates can exceed DataFusion internal grouping ID capacity; preserve explicit failures rather than silently deduplicating.

supplemental_protocol.why: Add several positive and negative 64-bit bitmap patterns beyond zero and all-ones.

combinations_protocol.why: Review actual grouping-key count for cross-products and repeated grouping expressions; keep the original 72-query corpus and 64-bit supplement unchanged.

implementation.rule: Mask duplicate ordinals out of the public ID while preserving duplicate result rows. Map full-width unsigned patterns to signed BIGINT with range-safe native CASE expressions. Deduplicate shared grouping-key metadata in first-appearance order for projection, HAVING and ORDER BY rewriting.
implementation.reuse: Existing native bitwise expressions, CASE and casts; stdlib HashSet for metadata. No new execution node, dependency or Python runtime path.

correctness.rust_unit_coverage: Both ANSI modes, signed 64-bit IDs, duplicate sets at storage-width boundaries, zero grouping keys, mixed ROLLUP and empty-input grand totals. Verify values, names, types and row multiplicity.

empty_input_semantic_policy.expected: Two grand-total rows, each with zero count and the semantic missing-key bitmask.
empty_input_semantic_policy.policy: Retain correct SQL semantics as authorized by the user.

attempt_00.reason_for_revision: The supplemental cross-product queries exposed duplicate keys in Sail grouping-function metadata. Retain first-appearance order while removing duplicate metadata entries.

iterations.validation_scope: The original 72-query corpus was frozen before implementation; the signed-bit supplement preceded initial candidate capture; the six combination queries were added afterward.

performance_protocol.purpose: Measure GROUPING_ID semantic-bit masking on an already-correct nonduplicate ROLLUP. Preserve identical values and native input work; keep ordinary grouping and projection controls.
performance_protocol.inference: Use process medians, paired quartet log ratios and fixed seed 172 / 10000 bootstrap resamples. Retain all controls and observations.
performance_protocol.runtime: 19705f2 optional runtime with one-file GROUPING_ID correction
performance_protocol.input_limit: 512 integer keys and a nonduplicate grand total produce 513 sorted IDs. Duplicate and full-width correctness is covered separately in the SQL corpus.

performance_findings: GROUPING_ID planning adds 8.988 percent, conditional interval [8.612,9.366], and 9.873 percent instructions. Process-median centers move from 0.660963 to 0.719737 ms. This local planning cost remains.

GROUPING_ID execution changes by 0.252 percent, interval [0.030,0.473], with 0.005 percent additional instructions. Its same-parent-binary control changes by -0.182 percent, interval [-0.302,-0.062]; the unchanged projection control rises 0.682 percent. These timing shifts do not establish a stable causal execution regression or universal equivalence.
Ordinary integer grouping and projection planning instruction changes are below 0.04 percent in magnitude; execution instruction changes are at most 0.001 percent.
All 160 processes and 41 samples per process retained, full counter coverage, zero migrations, unchanged governor and ASLR. No concurrent build or source investigation during measurement.
This comparison uses an already-correct nonduplicate integer ROLLUP with 513 output rows. It does not quantify full-width CASE performance or remove earlier floating normalization/widening costs.
limitations: 10 original observations exceed the native 64-bit capacity for semantic bits plus duplicate ordinals. This patch does not expand that capacity or deduplicate result rows.
6 original observations retain correct grand-total groups on empty input where Spark 4.2 returns no rows. These remain explicit Spark differences under the user-approved SQL semantic policy.
4 combination observations remain: repeated columns within a single ROLLUP produce a duplicate-field planning error, and ROLLUP nested inside GROUPING SETS is rejected by the parser.
The release-profile integration tests do not repair the separate native shift-by-64 panic under overflow checks. A focused Rust reproduction is recorded for a subsequent one-line native fix.
This slice does not remove floating grouping, dynamic integer widening or floating USING normalization costs. The optional type-inference shortcut remains unapplied.
Spark observation comparison checks values, types and error stages. Rust tests check selected names/types; real-Delta captures compare full schemas and captured rows.
